name: abs
description: Returns the absolute value of a number, removing any negative sign.

name: add
description: Adds two or more inputs element wise. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 0 before summing.
definition: add(x, y, filter = false), x + y

name: densify
description: Converts a grouping field of many buckets into lesser number of only available buckets so as to make working with grouping fields computationally efficient

name: divide
description: x / y

name: max
description: Maximum value of all inputs. At least 2 inputs are required

name: min
description: Minimum value of all inputs. At least 2 inputs are required

name: multiply
description: Multiplies two or more inputs element wise. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 0 before multiplication

name: power
description: x ^ y

name: reverse
description: - x

name: sign
description:
Returns the sign of a number: +1 for positive, -1 for negative, and 0 for zero. If the input is NaN, returns NaN.

Input: Value of 7 instruments at day t: (2, -3, 5, 6, 3, NaN, -10)
Output: (1, -1, 1, 1, 1, NaN, -1)

name: signed_power
description: x raised to the power of y such that final result preserves sign of x

name: subtract
description: Subtracts inputs left to right: x ? y ? … Supports two or more inputs. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 0 before subtraction.

name: log
description: Calculates the natural logarithm of the input value. Commonly used to transform data that has positive values.

name: sqrt
description: Returns the non negative square root of x. Equivalent to power(x, 0.5); for signed roots use signed_power(x, 0.5).

name: arc_cos
description: If -1 <= x <= 1: arccos(x); else NaN

name: arc_sin
description: If -1 <= x <= 1: arcsin(x); else NaN

name: arc_tan
description: This operator does inverse tangent of input

name: ceiling
description: Nearest larger integer

name: exp
description: Natural exponential function: e^x

name: floor
description: Nearest smaller integer

name: fraction
description: This operator removes the whole number part and returns the remaining fraction part with sign

name: log_diff
description: Returns log(current value of input or x[t] ) - log(previous value of input or x[t-1])

name: nan_mask
description: replace input with NAN if input's corresponding mask value or the second input here, is negative

name: nan_out
description: If x < lower or x > upper return NaN, else return x. At least one of "lower", "upper" is required

name: pasteurize
description:
Set to NaN if x is INF or if the underlying instrument is not in the Alpha universe. This operator may help reduce outliers.

Input: Value of 7 instruments at day t: (2, 3, 5, INF, 3, 8, 10), where value 10 does not belong in Alpha universe
Output: (2, 3, 5, NaN, 3, 8, NaN)

name: purify
description: Clear infinities (+inf, -inf) by replacing with NaN

name: replace
description: Replace target values in input with destination values

name: round
description: Round input to closest integer.

name: round_down
sigmoid
description: Returns 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

name: s_log_1p
description: Confine function to a shorter range using logarithm such that higher input remains higher and negative input remains negative as an output of resulting function and -1 or 1 is an asymptotic value

name: tanh
description: Hyperbolic tangent of x

name: to_nan
description: Convert value to NaN or NaN to value if reverse=true

name: and
description: Returns 1 ('true') if both inputs are 1 ('true'). Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

name: equal
description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 and input2 are the same. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

name: greater
description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a larger than input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

name: greater_equal
description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a larger or the same as input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

name: if_else
description: The if_else operator returns one of two values based on a condition. If the condition is true, it returns the first value; if false, it returns the second value.

name: is_nan
description: If (input == NaN) return 1 else return 0

name: less_equal
description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a smaller or the same as input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

name: not
description: Returns the logical negation of x. Returns 0 when x is 1 (‘true’) and 1 when x is 0 (‘false’).

name: not_equal
description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 and input2 are different numbers. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

name: or
description: Returns 1 if either input is true (either input1 or input2 has a value of 1), otherwise it returns 0.

name: less
description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a smaller than input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

name: is_finite
description: If (input NaN or input == INF) return 0, else return 1

name: is_not_finite
description: If (input NAN or input == INF) return 1 else return 0

name: is_not_nan
description: If (input != NaN) return 1 else return 0

name: negate
description: The result is true if the converted operand is false; the result is false if the converted operand is true

name: days_from_last_change
description: Calculates the number of days since the last change in the value of a given variable.

name: hump
description: Limits amount and magnitude of changes in input (thus reducing turnover)

name: last_diff_value
description: Returns the most recent value of x from the past d days that is different from the current value of x.

name: ts_arg_max
description: Returns the number of days since the maximum value occurred in the last d days of a time series. If today's value is the maximum, returns 0; if it was yesterday, returns 1, and so on.

name: ts_arg_min
description: Returns the number of days since the minimum value occurred in a time series over the past d days. If today's value is the minimum, returns 0; if it was yesterday, returns 1, and so on.

name: ts_av_diff
description: Calculates the difference between a value and its mean over a specified period, ignoring NaN values in the mean calculation. In short, it returns x – ts_mean(x, d) with NaNs ignored.

name: ts_backfill
description: Replaces missing (NaN) values in a time series with the most recent valid value from a specified lookback window, improving data coverage and reducing risk from missing data.

name: ts_delay
description: Returns the value of a variable x from d days ago. Use this operator to access historical data points by specifying the desired time lag in days.

name: ts_delta
description: Calculates the difference between a value and its delayed version over a specified period. Useful for measuring changes or momentum in time-series data.

name: ts_mean
description: Calculates the simple average (mean) value of a variable x over the past d days.

name: ts_quantile
description: Calculates the ts_rank of the input and transforms it using the inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile function) of a specified probability distribution (default: Gaussian/normal). This helps to normalize or reshape the distribution of your data over a rolling window.

name: ts_rank
description: Ranks the value of a variable for each instrument over a specified number of past days, returning the rank of the current value (optionally adjusted by a constant). Useful for normalizing time-series data and highlighting relative performance over time.

name: ts_scale
description: Scales a time series to a 0–1 range based on its minimum and maximum values over a specified period, with an optional constant shift.

name: ts_std_dev
description: Calculates the standard deviation of a data series x over the past d days, measuring how much the values deviate from their mean during that period.

name: ts_sum
description: Sum values of x for the past d days.

name: ts_zscore
description: Calculates the Z-score of a time series, showing how far today's value is from the recent average, measured in standard deviations. Useful for standardizing and comparing values over time.

name: kth_element
description: Returns the K-th value from a time series by looking back over a specified number of (‘d’) days, with the option to ignore certain values. Commonly used for backfilling missing data.

name: ts_corr
description: Calculates the Pearson correlation between two variables, x and y, over the past d days, showing how closely they move together.

name: ts_count_nans
description: Counts the number of missing (NaN) values in a data series over a specified number of days.

name: ts_covariance
description: Calculates the covariance between two time-series variables, y and x, over the past d days. Useful for measuring how two variables move together within a specified historical window.

name: ts_decay_linear
description: Applies a linear decay to time-series data over a set number of days, smoothing the data by averaging recent values and reducing the impact of older or missing data.

name: ts_product
description: Returns the product of the values of x over the past d days. Useful for calculating geometric means and compounding returns or growth rates.

name: ts_regression
description: Returns various parameters related to regression function

name: ts_step
description: Returns a counter of days, incrementing by one each day.

name: hump_decay
description: This operator helps to ignore the values that changed too little corresponding to previous ones

name: inst_tvr
description:
Total trading value / Total holding value in the past d days

Input: Value of 1 instrument in past 5 days where first element is the latest: (105, 102, 99, 101,100)
Output: 0.022 from (1+2+3+3)/(105+102+99+101)

name: jump_decay
description: If there is a huge jump in current data compare to previous one

name: ts_co_kurtosis
description: Returns cokurtosis of y and x for the past d days

name: ts_co_skewness
description: Returns coskewness of y and x for the past d days

name: ts_decay_exp_window
description: Returns exponential decay of x with smoothing factor for the past d days

name: ts_delta_limit
description: Limit the change in the Alpha position x between dates to a specified fraction of y. The "limit_volume" can be in the range of 0 to 1. Also, please be aware of the scaling for x and y. Besides setting y as adv20 or volume related data, you can also set y as a constant.

name: ts_entropy
description: For each instrument, we collect values of input in the past d days and calculate the probability distribution then the information entropy via a histogram as a result

name: ts_ir
description: Return information ratio ts_mean(x, d) / ts_std_dev(x, d)

name: ts_kurtosis
description: Returns kurtosis of x for the last d days

name: ts_max
description: Returns max value of x for the past d days

name: ts_max_diff
description: Returns x - ts_max(x, d)

name: ts_median
description: Returns median value of x for the past d days

name: ts_min
description: Returns min value of x for the past d days

name: ts_min_diff
description: Returns x - ts_min(x, d)

name: ts_min_max_cps
description: Returns (ts_min(x, d) + ts_max(x, d)) - f * x. If not specified, by default f = 2

name: ts_min_max_diff
description: Returns x - f * (ts_min(x, d) + ts_max(x, d)). If not specified, by default f = 0.5

name: ts_moment
description: Returns K-th central moment of x for the past d days

name: ts_partial_corr
description: Returns partial correlation of x, y, z for the past d days

name: ts_percentage
description: Returns percentile value of x for the past d days

name: ts_poly_regression
description: Returns y - Ey, where Ey = x + x^2 + ... + x^k over d days; k must be specified as a keyword argument

name: ts_rank_gmean_amean_diff
description: Returns Geometric Mean of ts_rank(input,d) of all input - Arithmetic Mean of ts_rank(input,d) of all input. This is similar to rank_gmean_amean_diff operator but in time-series space

name: ts_returns
description: Returns the relative change in the x value

name: ts_skewness
description: Return skewness of x for the past d days

name: ts_target_tvr_delta_limit
description: Tune "ts_delta_limit" to have a turnover equal to a certain target with optimization weight range between lambda_min, lambda_max. Also, please be aware of the scaling for x and y. Besides setting y as adv20 or volume related data, you can also set y as a constant.

name: ts_target_tvr_hump
description: Tune "hump" to have a turnover equal to a certain target with optimization weight range between lambda_min, lambda_max.

name: ts_theilsen
description: Theil Sen slope estimator of inputs for the past n days.

name: ts_triple_corr
description: Returns triple correlation of x, y, z for the past d days

name: ts_vector_neut
description: Returns x- ts_vector_proj(x,y,d)

name: ts_vector_proj
description: Returns vector projection of x onto y in time-series space.

name: ts_weighted_decay
description: Instead of replacing today's value with yesterday's as in ts_decay(x, 1), it assigns weighted average of today's and yesterday's values with weight on today's value being k and yesterday's being (1-k)

name: ts_target_tvr_decay
description: Tune "ts_decay" to have a turnover equal to a certain target, with optimization weight range between lambda_min, lambda_max

name: normalize
description: Calculates the mean value of all valid alpha values for a certain date, then subtracts that mean from each element

name: quantile
description: Rank the raw vector, shift the ranked Alpha vector, apply distribution (gaussian, cauchy, uniform). If driver is uniform, it simply subtract each Alpha value with the mean of all Alpha values in the Alpha vector

name: rank
description: Ranks the input among all the instruments and returns an equally distributed number between 0.0 and 1.0. For precise sort, use the rate as 0

name: scale
description: Scales input to booksize. We can also scale the long positions and short positions to separate scales by mentioning additional parameters to the operator

name: winsorize
description:
Winsorizes x to make sure that all values in x are between the lower and upper limits, which are specified as multiple of std.

Input: Value of 7 instruments at day t: (2, 4, 5, 6, 3, 8, 10), std: 1
Output: (2.81, 4, 5, 6, 3, 8, 8.03) from SD. = 2.61, mean = 5.42

name: zscore
description: Z-score is a numerical measurement that describes a value's relationship to the mean of a group of values. Z-score is measured in terms of standard deviations from the mean

name: multi_regression
description:
Perform multivariable regression of multiple independent variables (x1,x2,...) on a dependent variable (y) across number of days.

If days = n (n >= 0), will include past n days in the regression. Setting days = 0 indicates that we're only using today (x1, x2, ...) to predict y.

If lag = m (m >= 0), will lag (x1, x2, ...) for m days for prediction.

Options for solver: "SVD"(default), "QR", "NORMAL"
definition: multi_regression(y, x1, x2,..., days=0, lag=0, solver="SVD")

name: generalized_rank
description: The idea is that difference between instrument values raised to the power of m is added to the rank of instrument with bigger value and subtracted from the rank of instrument with lesser value. More details in the notes at the end of page

name: one_side
description: Shifts all instruments up or down so that the Alpha becomes long-only or short-only (if side = short), respectively.

name: rank_by_side
description: Ranks positive and negative input separately and scale to book. For precise sorting use rate=0

name: rank_gmean_amean_diff
description: Operator returns difference of geometric mean and arithmetic mean of cross sectional rank of inputs

name: regression_neut
description: Conducts the cross-sectional regression on the stocks with Y as target and X as the independent variable

name: regression_proj
description: Conducts the cross-sectional regression on the stocks with Y as target and X as the independent variable

name: scale_down
description: Scales all values in each day proportionately between 0 and 1 such that minimum value maps to 0 and maximum value maps to 1. Constant is the offset by which final result is subtracted

name: truncate
description: Operator truncates all values of x to maxPercent. Here, maxPercent is in decimal notation

name: vector_neut
description: For given vectors x and y, it finds a new vector x* (output) such that x* is orthogonal to y

name: vector_proj
description: Returns vector projection of x onto y.

name: vec_avg
description:
Taking mean of the vector field x

Input: Vector of value of 1 instrument in a day: (2, 3, 5, 6, 3, 8, 10)
Output: 37 / 7 = 5.29

name: vec_sum
description:
Sum of vector field x

Input: Vector of value of 1 instrument in a day: (2, 3, 5, 6, 3, 8, 10)
Output: 2 + 3 + 5 + 6 + 3 + 8 + 10 = 37

name: vec_choose
description: Choosing k-th item(indexed at 0) from each vector field x

name: vec_count
description: Number of elements in vector field x

name: vec_filter
description: Filter vector by values, such as nan. Can filter many values at once, for example: vec_filter(vec, value="nan 0 10"). Please note the output of this VECTOR will still be vector data.

name: vec_ir
description: Information Ratio (Mean / Standard Deviation) of vector field x

name: vec_kurtosis
description: Kurtosis of vector field x

name: vec_max
description: Maximum value form vector field x

name: vec_min
description: Minimum value form vector field x

name: vec_norm
description: Sum of all absolute values of vector field x

name: vec_percentage
description: Percentile of vector field x

name: vec_powersum
description: Sum of power of vector field x

name: vec_range
description: Difference between maximum and minimum element in vector field x

name: vec_skewness
description: Skewness of vector field x

name: vec_stddev
description: Standard Deviation of vector field x

name: bucket
description: Convert float values into indexes for user-specified buckets. Bucket is useful for creating group values, which can be passed to GROUP as input

name: generate_stats
description: The generate_stats() operator calculates Alpha statistics for each day in the IS period. It takes an input of selected Alphas with shape = (A x D x I). It outputs daily statistics for each Alpha with shape = (S x D x A), where S is the number of statistics calculated.

name: trade_when
description: Used in order to change Alpha values only under a specified condition and to hold Alpha values in other cases. It also allows to close Alpha positions (assign NaN values) under a specified condition

name: clamp
description: Limits input value between lower and upper bound in inverse = false mode (which is default). Alternatively, when inverse = true, values between bounds are replaced with mask, while values outside bounds are left as is
definition: clamp(x, lower = 0, upper = 0, inverse = False, mask = )

name: filter
description: Used to filter the value and allows to create filters like linear or exponential decay

name: keep
description: This operator outputs value x when f changes and continues to do that for "period" days after f stopped changing. After "period" days since last change of f, NaN is output

name: left_tail
description: NaN everything greater than maximum, maximum should be constant

name: right_tail
description: NaN everything less than minimum, minimum should be constant

name: tail
description: If (x > lower AND x < upper) return newval, else return x. Lower, upper, newval should be constants

name: group_backfill
description: If a certain value for a certain date and instrument is NaN, from the set of same group instruments, calculate winsorized mean of all non-NaN values over last d days

name: group_mean
description: All elements in group equals to the mean

name: group_neutralize
description: Neutralizes Alpha against groups. These groups can be subindustry, industry, sector, country or a constant

name: group_rank
description: Each elements in a group is assigned the corresponding rank in this group

name: group_zscore
description:
Calculates group Z-score - numerical measurement that describes a value's relationship to the mean of a group of values. Z-score is measured in terms of standard deviations from the mean. zscore = (data - mean) / stddev of x for each instrument within its group.

Input: Value of 5 instruments of Group A: (100, 0, 50, 60, 25)
Output: (1.57, -1.39, 0.09, 0.39, -0.65)

name: combo_a
description:
Combines multiple alpha signals into a single weighted output by balancing each alpha's historical return with its variability over the most recent nlength days.

The parameter mode selects one of the several weighted approaches (algo1, algo2, algo3), each of which handles the tradeoff between performance and stability differently.

name: group_scale
description: Normalizes the values in a group to be between 0 and 1. (x - groupmin) / (groupmax - groupmin)

name: group_cartesian_product
description: Merge two groups into one group. If originally there are len_1 and len_2 group indices in g1 and g2, there will be len_1 * len_2 indices in the new group.

name: group_coalesce
description: Regroup remaining stocks based on group2 and so on if original_group does not cover all stocks in target universe

name: group_count
description: Gives the number of instruments in the same group (e.g. sector) which have valid values of x. For example, x=1 gives the number of instruments in each group (without regard for whether any particular field has valid data). This operator improves weight coverage and may help to reduce drawdown risk.

name: group_extra
description: Replaces NaN values by their corresponding group means.

name: group_max
description: Maximum of x for all instruments in the same group.

name: group_median
description: All elements in group equals to the median value of the group.

name: group_min
description: All elements in group equals to the min value of the group.

name: group_normalize
description: Normalizes input such that each group's absolute sum is 1

name: group_percentage
description: All elements in group equals to the value over the percentage of the group. Percentage = 0.5 means value is equal to group_median(x, group)

name: group_std_dev
description: All elements in group equals to the standard deviation of the group.

name: group_sum
description: Sum of x for all instruments in the same group.

name: group_vector_neut
description: Similar to vector_neut(x, y) but x neutralize to y for each group g which can be any classifier such as subindustry, industry, sector, etc.

name: group_vector_proj
description: Similar to vector_proj(x, y) but x projection to y for each group which can be any classifier such as subindustry, industry, sector, etc.

name: group_multi_regression
description:
Perform multivariable regression for each data points in a group. For more information, please refer to multi_regression.

Options for solver: "SVD"(default), "QR", "NORMAL"
definition: group_multi_regression(y, x1, x2, ..., group, days=0, lag=0, solver="SVD")

name: self_corr
description: Taking an input matrix of (D x N) with lookback="K", producing an output matrix of (D x N x N), where each output(di, j, k) refers to correlation of input(di-K:di, j) and input(di-K:di, k). Outputs (D x N x N) from the input of (D x N)

name: in
description: in

name: universe_size
description: universe_size

name: convert
description: Convert dollars to share or share to dollar when mode = "share2dollar". Please note that the use of the convert() operator in an Alpha Expression is considered as utilizing the pv1 dataset (Price Volume Data for Equity) since it relies on pv1 data for calculations

name: inst_pnl
description: Generate pnl per instruments. Please note that the use of the inst_pnl() operator in an Alpha Expression is considered as utilizing the pv1 dataset (Price Volume Data for Equity) since it relies on pv1 data for calculations.

name: reduce_avg
description: Average of non-NAN elements of d(..., :). Threshold: Minimum required number of valid (non-nan) values. If there is not enough valid values, then the output is nan. 0 means no limit.threshold (Default: 0) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_choose
description: Choose the 'nth' element in the array, return NAN if not found. Threshold: nth="<the Nth element>" (Required) ignoreNan="true|false" (Default: true) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_count
description: Count the number of element of d(..., :) > threshold. threshold=<float> *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_ir
description: IR of values in the array *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_kurtosis
description:
Kurtosis of values in the array ***Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. 
If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) 
If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) 
The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_max
description: Maximum of elements of d(..., :) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_min
description:
Minimum of elements of d(..., :) ***Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. 
If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) 
If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) 
The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_norm
description: Absolute sum of number of element of d(..., :) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_percentage
description: Return the value of percentage in the sorted array: e.g., median value when percentage=0.5. Threshold: percentage="<value between 0 and 1>" (Default: 0.5) *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_powersum
description: Sum of power, sum(power(x, constant)). Threshold: precise, whether calculate power precise if constant greater than 4, default false constant=<integer value>, default:2 *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_range
description: Return the range of values in the array, return NAN if no valid value *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_skewness
description: Skewness of values in the array *** Takes an input 2-D or 3-D matrix with user-defined reducer, producing an output matrix. *If input matrix is (D x N), output matrix (D x 1) *If input matrix is (D x N X N), output matrix (D x N X 1) *The defined function is applied on the last dimension : output(I) = reduce(input(I, 0:N)).

name: reduce_stddev
description: Standard deviation of values in the array. Threshold: Minimum required percentage of valid (non-nan) values.
